items.title: Section: Ten Names for Contemplation — Why the Buddha's Titles Shrank From Ten Thousand to Ten

items.zh: 又諸如來略有十種功德名號隨念功德。何等為十？謂薄伽梵，號為如來、應、正等覺、明行圓滿、善逝、世間解、無上丈夫調御士、天人師、佛、薄伽梵。
items.en: Tathāgatas may, in brief, be contemplated through ten kinds of virtuous names. What are these ten? The Blessed One is named: Tathāgata, Worthy One, Perfectly Enlightened One, Perfect in Wisdom and Conduct, Well-Gone One, Knower of the World, Unsurpassed Guide Who Tames Others, Teacher of Gods and Humans, Buddha, and Blessed One.

items.title: The First Three Names: Tathāgata, Worthy One, and Perfectly Enlightened

items.en: Because their words contain no falsehood whatsoever, they are called Tathāgata.

items.zh: 已得一切所應得義，應作世間無上福田，應為一切恭敬供養，是故名應。
items.en: Having attained every genuine benefit worth attaining, fit to serve as the world's unsurpassed field of merit, worthy of reverence and offerings from all beings — for this reason, they are called Worthy One.

items.title: Names Three Through Five: Perfectly Enlightened, Perfect in Wisdom and Conduct, and Well-Gone

items.zh: 如其勝義覺諸法故，名正等覺。明謂三明，行如經說止觀二品。極善圓滿，是故說名明行圓滿。
items.en: Because they are awakened to every phenomenon exactly as its ultimate truth actually is, they are called Perfectly Enlightened. "Wisdom" refers to the three knowledges; "conduct" refers, as the scriptures say, to calm-abiding and insight together. Both are brought to the most excellent completion — hence the name Perfect in Wisdom and Conduct.

items.zh: 上昇最極，永不退還，故名善逝。
items.en: Having risen to the very summit, they never fall back again — hence the name Well-Gone.

items.title: Names Six and Seven: Knower of the World, and the Unsurpassed Guide

items.zh: 善知世界及有情界一切品類染淨相故，名世間解。
items.en: Because they thoroughly understand every pure and defiled variety found throughout the physical world and the world of sentient beings, they are called Knower of the World.

items.zh: 一切世間唯一丈夫，善知最勝調心方便，是故說名無上丈夫調御士。
items.en: The one and only great being throughout the entire world, skilled in the most excellent means of taming the mind — for this reason, they are called the Unsurpassed Guide Who Tames Others.

items.title: Section: Teacher of Gods and Humans — Four Qualities That Make a Genuine Teacher

items.zh: 為實眼故，為實智故，為實義故，為實法故，與顯了義為開導故，與一切義為所依故，與不了義為能了故，與所生疑為能斷故，與甚深處為能顯故，令明淨故，與一切法為根本故，為開導故，為所依故，能正教誡教授天人，令其出離一切眾苦，是故說佛名天人師。
items.en: Because of genuine seeing, because of genuine wisdom, because of genuine meaning, and because of genuine teaching — opening the way so that meaning becomes manifest, serving as the basis for every meaning, clarifying what is not yet clear, resolving doubts that arise, and revealing what is most profound ... correctly instructing and teaching gods and humans, leading them out of every form of suffering — for this reason, the Buddha is called the Teacher of Gods and Humans.

items.title: Section: "Buddha" — Equal Awakening to What Helps, What Harms, and What Merely Passes the Time

items.zh: 於能引攝義利法聚，於能引攝非義利法聚，於能引攝非義利非非義利法聚，遍一切種現前等覺，故名為佛。
items.en: With respect to phenomena that lead to genuine benefit, phenomena that lead to genuine harm, and phenomena that lead to neither benefit nor harm, they are completely and equally awakened in every respect — for this reason, they are called Buddha.

items.title: Section: Blessed One — Defeating Four Great Māras, Closing All Ten Names

items.zh: 能破諸魔大力軍眾，具多功德，名薄伽梵。
items.en: Able to defeat every great army of māras, and possessing manifold virtues — this is called Blessed One.

items.zh: 或有多劫，無有一佛出現於世；或有一劫，有眾多佛出現於世。彼彼十方無量無數諸世界中，應知同時有無量佛出現於世。何以故？於十方界，現有無量無數菩薩，同時發願、同勤修集菩提資糧。若一菩薩，於如是日、於如是分、於如是月、於如是年發菩提心，願趣菩提。即於此日、即於此分、即於此月、即於此年，一切亦爾。如一菩薩勇悍策勵，熾然精進，一切亦爾。

items.title: Section: Countless Buddhas Appear at Once Across Countless Worlds — But Never Two in the Same One

items.zh: 於今現見此世界中，多百菩薩同時發願、同修惠施、同修淨戒、同修忍辱、同修精進、同修靜慮、同修智慧，況於十方無量無邊諸佛世界。
items.en: It can presently be observed that, in this very world, hundreds of bodhisattvas simultaneously generate the resolve and simultaneously cultivate giving, moral discipline, patience, diligence, concentration, and wisdom together — how much more so throughout the ten directions' immeasurable, boundless buddha-worlds.

items.zh: 又於十方現有無量無數三千大千佛土，無二菩薩同時修集菩提資糧，俱時圓滿，於一佛土並出於世，一時成佛，況有無量無數菩薩於一世界一時成佛。又不應言：眾多菩薩同時修集菩提資糧，俱時圓滿，前後相避，次第成佛。亦不應言：一切菩薩皆不成佛。
是故當知眾多菩薩同時修集菩提資糧俱圓滿者，於十方面無量無數隨其所淨空無如來諸佛國土，各別出世，同時成佛。
items.en: For this reason, it should be understood that when many bodhisattvas simultaneously complete gathering the provisions for awakening together, they each separately appear in the world, becoming buddhas at the same time, each within whichever immeasurable, uncountable buddha-land throughout the ten directions currently has no Tathāgata and matches the purification they themselves have cultivated.

items.zh: 由此道理，多世界中，決定應有眾多菩薩同時成佛。決定無有一佛土中，有二如來俱時出世。何以故？

items.title: Section: Why Exactly One Buddha Per World — Three Reasons, and the Wisdom of Scarcity

items.zh: 菩薩長夜起如是願，隨令增長：我當獨一，於無導首諸世界中，為作導首，調伏有情，令脫眾苦、令般涅槃。如是長夜所起大願隨令增長，攝受正行得成滿故，無二如來於一世界俱時出現。又一如來，於一三千大千佛土，普能施作一切佛事，是故第二如來出世無所利益。
items.en: Across the long night of saṃsāra, a bodhisattva generates and continually strengthens this very vow: "I alone shall become the guide within whatever world currently has no guide of its own." ... Moreover, a single Tathāgata, within a single great trichiliocosm, is universally able to accomplish every buddha-activity needed there — and so a second Tathāgata appearing in that same world would bring no further benefit at all.

items.zh: 又一如來，於一佛土出現於世，令諸有情成辦自義，極為熾盛、極為隨順。何以故？
彼作是思：一切世間唯一如來，更無第二。若於此土化事已訖，或往餘方，或入滅度。我等何從當修梵行？我等何從當聞正法？如是思已，發起深厚欲勤精進，速修梵行、速聞正法。若一佛土多佛出世，彼於所作不能速疾。
items.en: Beings reflect in this way: "Throughout the entire world there is only this one Tathāgata, and no second one. If his work of teaching in this land should ever come to an end, whether by departing elsewhere or by entering final nirvāṇa, from whom shall we then learn the pure conduct of the path? From whom shall we then hear the true teaching?" Reflecting in this way, they arouse deep, earnest diligence ... whereas if a single buddha-land had many buddhas appearing in it, beings would not be swift in their own efforts at all.

items.zh: 故一佛土一佛出世，令諸有情成辦自義，極為熾盛、極為隨順。

blocks.text: The ten classical titles of the Buddha, each explained, and the question of whether more than one Buddha can appear at once. Two short passages (0499c10, 0499c22) are untranslated.

items: **Tathāgata**: "because their words contain no falsehood". Venerable Miào Jìng: 如 here means "true".
**Worthy One** (arhat): "worthy of reverence and offerings from all beings".
**Perfectly Enlightened**: "awakened to every phenomenon exactly as its ultimate truth is".
**Perfect in Wisdom and Conduct**: wisdom is the three knowledges; conduct, calm and insight.
**Well-Gone**: "having risen to the very summit, never falling back".
**Knower of the World**: of "every pure and defiled variety in the physical world and the world of beings".
**Unsurpassed Guide Who Tames Others**: "skilled in the most excellent means of taming the mind".
**Teacher of Gods and Humans**: through "genuine seeing, wisdom, meaning, and teaching".
**Buddha**: "equally awakened to what leads to benefit, to harm, and to neither".
**Blessed One**: "able to defeat every army of Māras, and possessing manifold virtues".

blocks.text: "In this very world, hundreds of bodhisattvas simultaneously generate the resolve and practise." So when many complete the provisions together, "they each appear in the world, becoming Buddhas at the same time", in different worlds.

Three reasons there is only one Buddha in a world: the bodhisattva's long vow, "I alone shall become the guide in a world that has none"; a single Tathāgata is enough for all the work there; and scarcity inspires effort: "There is only this one Tathāgata; if he departs, from whom shall we hear the Dharma?"

quiz.q: "Tathāgatas have, in brief, ten virtuous names." Why "in brief," per Venerable Miào Jìng?
options: this is brief — in full, the Buddha has boundless names
quiz.why: "Tathāgatas may, in brief, be contemplated through ten kinds of virtuous names." Venerable Miào Jìng: this is the brief account; in full, the Buddha has boundless names.

quiz.q: "Because their words contain no falsehood, they are called Tathāgata." How do the masters read 如 here?
options: Miào Jìng: 如 means truthfulness; Cháng Bǎi: the Diamond Sūtra speaks of the dharma-body "coming from nowhere"; here it's about virtue — no false words
quiz.why: "Because their words contain no falsehood whatsoever, they are called Tathāgata." Venerable Miào Jìng: 如 here is to be read as truthfulness. Master Cháng Bǎi: the Diamond Sūtra speaks of the dharma-body — "coming from nowhere, going nowhere, hence Tathāgata"; here it's said in terms of virtue.

quiz.q: In "Perfect in Wisdom and Conduct," wisdom is "the three knowledges." What does each counter, per Master Cháng Bǎi?
options: past-lives counters eternalism, divine eye annihilationism, extinction the view of present-life nirvāṇa
quiz.why: "'Wisdom' refers to the three knowledges; 'conduct' refers, as the scriptures say, to calm-abiding and insight together." Master Cháng Bǎi: the knowledge of past lives counters eternalism; the divine eye counters annihilationism; the extinction of contaminants counters the view of nirvāṇa in this life.

quiz.q: Teacher of gods and humans: "與顯了義為開導" — rendered "guiding through what is already clear." What do the lectures say?
options: Miào Jìng: first opening, then clarity — the eye's function; Cháng Bǎi: genuine eye and wisdom concern the knower, genuine meaning and teaching the known
quiz.why: "Because of genuine seeing, because of genuine wisdom, because of genuine meaning, and because of genuine teaching — guiding through what is already clear." Venerable Miào Jìng: first there must be opening, then clarity — that's the eye's function. Master Cháng Bǎi: genuine eye and wisdom are said of the knowing wisdom; genuine meaning and teaching of the known object. "Already clear" doesn't fit.

quiz.q: "Completely and equally awakened in every respect — hence Buddha." How does Venerable Miào Jìng explain "present, equal awakening"?
options: no reference, no thinking needed — he knows at once
quiz.why: "They are completely and equally awakened in every respect — for this reason, they are called Buddha." Venerable Miào Jìng: no need to consult anything or think it over — he knows immediately.

quiz.q: Many bodhisattvas complete their provisions together and "appear separately in buddha-lands with no Tathāgata." What does Master Cháng Bǎi say?
options: once complete, each goes to a buddha-less world matching the pure land they cultivated
quiz.why: "When many bodhisattvas simultaneously complete gathering the provisions for awakening together, they each separately appear in the world … in whichever buddha-land currently has no Tathāgata and matches the purification they themselves have cultivated." Master Cháng Bǎi: once a bodhisattva's provisions are complete, he goes to a currently buddha-less world matching the pure land he cultivated long ago, and becomes a buddha there.

quiz.q: "The bodhisattva generates this vow and 隨令增長" — rendered "continually strengthens." What do the lectures say?
options: Miào Jìng: 增長 here means "definite, resolved"; Cháng Bǎi: one buddha suffices to guide beings
quiz.why: "Across the long night of saṃsāra, a bodhisattva generates and continually strengthens this very vow: 'I alone shall become the guide.'" Venerable Miào Jìng: I think 增長 here means "decided." Master Cháng Bǎi: guiding beings needs just one buddha. The English "strengthens" differs from Miào Jìng's reading.
